title: Private IP Addresses
description: Free addresses that never touch the Internet directly
tagline: Free addresses that never touch the Internet directly

sections.title: What "Private" Means
sections.body: Three ranges were reserved for anyone to use inside their own networks — free of charge, no permission needed. They are NOT routable on the Internet; routers on the Internet simply drop them.

sections.title: How Private IPs Reach the Internet: NAT
sections.body: Your router keeps a private IP inside and swaps it for its PUBLIC IP when traffic leaves (NAT — Network Address Translation). Replies come back to the public IP, and the router sends them to the right private device.

sections.title: Why This Saved the Internet
sections.body: Billions of devices share millions of public IPs thanks to private + NAT. Every home Wi-Fi reuses 192.168.1.x — that is fine because those packets never appear on the Internet with those addresses.
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: memorize the three ranges exactly. 172 range starts at 172.16 — not 172.0!
